hero.title: Mechanical Engineering in France
hero.subtitle: France is a great country for students who want to Study postgraduate in mechanical engineering\. French universities and engineering schools have master's programs with a focus on fields such as advanced manufacturing, robotics, automotive engineering, aerospace technology, materials science, energy systems and product design.

overview: The Branch of engineering that deals with the design, development, analysis, and production of machinery, mechanical systems, and industrial equipment is known as mechanical engineering. In France, university masters and engineering-school education give the opportunity to postgraduate students to discover advanced engineering technologies.
Advanced engineering specialisations: You can choose from automotive, aerospace, robotics, mechatronics, manufacturing and energy systems.
Research and innovation: Students can use research laboratories and take part in projects on advanced materials, mechanical design, automation and industrial technologies.

sections.title: Why study a Mechanical Engineering PG in France?
sections.lead: The Branch of engineering that deals with the design, development, analysis, and production of machinery, mechanical systems, and industrial equipment is known as mechanical engineering. In France, university masters and engineering-school education give the opportunity to postgraduate students to discover advanced engineering technologies.

items: Advanced engineering specialisations: You can choose from automotive, aerospace, robotics, mechatronics, manufacturing and energy systems.
Research and innovation: Students can use research laboratories and take part in projects on advanced materials, mechanical design, automation and industrial technologies.
Industry oriented learning: Selected programs offer internships, technical projects and work-study opportunities.
Modern engineering facilities: Laboratories, simulation tools and special engineering equipment allow students to acquire practical knowledge.
International learning environment: French institutions attract students from all over the world and offer selected programs in English.
European career exposure: Students may explore engineering careers across France and other European countries, subject to employment requirements and work authorization.
More academic opportunities: A relevant master's degree can open the door to doctoral studies and specialized research.

sections.title: Postgraduate Mechanical Engineering Courses in France
sections.lead: The title of all relevant French postgraduate programs may not include the term \\Mechanical Engineering\. Candidates should also explore Masters degrees in mechanical systems, industrial engineering, materials science, energy engineering and mechatronics.

items: Popular Specializations are:
\\Mechanical Engineering:\\ Advanced machine design, mechanical systems, engineering analysis, and product development.
\\Automotive Engineering\\: Vehicle design, automotive systems, electric vehicles, and mobility technologies.
\\Aerospace Engineering:\\ Aircraft structure, propulsion systems, aerodynamics, aerospace materials.
\\Robotics and Automation:\\ Industrial robots, automatic production, control systems, smart machines.
\\Mechatronics Engineering:\\ Integration of mechanical systems, electronics, sensors and control technologies.
\\Manufacturing Engineering:\\ Production systems, advanced manufacturing, industrial processes and quality control.
\\Materials Engineering:\\ Composites, polymers, metals, material properties, applications of advanced materials.
\\Energy Engineering:\\ Thermal systems, renewable energy technologies, energy efficiency and sustainable design.
\\Computational Mechanics\\ Numerical simulation, finite element analysis, fluid mechanics, mechanical modeling.
\\Product Design & Development:\\ Engineering design, prototyping, product testing and innovation.
In France, a national Master's degree is normally two years long after a related bachelor's degree and awards 120 ECTS credits over the master's cycle.
Candidates with suitable academic background may be admitted directly to the second year in some institutions.

sections.title: Eligibility to Study Pg in Mechanical Engineering in France
sections.lead: Applicants generally need a relevant undergraduate qualification and sufficient knowledge of mathematics, physics, and engineering fundamentals.

items: Common \\eligibility requirements for mechanical engineering PG in France\\ are:
A recognized \\Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering\\ or \\Automobile Engineering\\ or \\Aerospace Engineering\\ or \\Production Engineering\\ or a related field.
A \\BTech\\, \\BE\\, BSc or equivalent qualification, depending on the program.
Good academic background in undergraduate engineering courses.
Engineering Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Fluid Mechanics, Materials Science and Mathematics as per the specialization.
Proficiency in English language for English-taught programs.
French language proficiency\\ for courses taught in French.
Other academic or technical requirements as may be specified by the institution.

sections.title: Admission Requirements
sections.lead: In France, each university of engineering has its own admission policy and evaluates applications accordingly.

items: Below are the \\common admission requirements for PG in mechanical engineering in France\\:
Bachelor's degree certificate or provisional certificate.
Academic transcripts (official).
CV (Curriculum vitae).
Statement of purpose (SOP) / Letter of motivation.
Results of the English language test, if required.
Proof of French language skills for programs taught in French.
Letters of recommendation if needed.
Valid passport or other acceptable identification.
Internship certificates / work experience documents (if applicable)
Research proposal or technical portfolio for the selected programs.
Interview or technical test if needed.
Some programs may require knowledge of \\mechanical design\\, \\thermodynamics\\, \\fluid mechanics\\, \\manufacturing processes\\, \\CAD software\\ or engineering mathematics.

sections.title: Cost of living
sections.lead: Students should expect to pay for housing, food, transportation, books, engineering supplies, computers, health fees and other personal costs.

items: Cost of living in France depends on the city you live in and the type of accommodation you choose. Larger student cities may have higher costs for housing and transportation than smaller ones.
Students can find out more about \\scholarships in France\\, the institutional financial aid and the work-study programs they can benefit from to help them cope with their education costs.

sections.title: Admission Procedure
sections.lead: The \\admission procedure for mechanical engineering PG in France\\ differs depending on the university, program, nationality, and current residing country.

items: 1. \\Pick a specialisation\\ Decide if you want mechanical design, automotive engineering, robotics, aerospace engineering, manufacturing or one of the other related fields.
2. \\Shortlist universities:\\ Compare universities and engineering schools by course content, teaching language, tuition fees and career opportunities.
3. \\Check eligibility:\\ Ensure your bachelor's degree and previous engineering subjects meet the programme's requirements.
4. \\Know the application platform:\\ Depending on the program, the application may be submitted through the university portal or an alternative system.
5. \\Prepare your documents:\\ Obtain your academic transcripts, degree certificates, CV, statement of purpose or motivation letter and language-test scores.
6. \\Apply:\\ Complete the application process and meet all official deadlines.
7. \\Stages of the selection process:\\ You may be invited for interviews or asked to provide additional technical documents.
8. \\Accept the offer of admission:\\ Follow the university's enrollment instructions and payment requirements.
9. \\Arrive ready:\\ Complete all the required \\formalities for the French student visa\\ and arrange accommodation.

sections.title: Accreditation and Recognition
sections.lead: Students are advised to check the qualification awarded and its recognition prior to enrollment.

items: A national Master's degree is part of the French and European higher education system.
Before applying, students should verify the following:
The exact title of your degree and the awarding institution.
The qualification is a national Master's degree or an engineering diploma.
Duration of the program and ECTS credits.
Current accreditation status as applicable.
Internship, lab and research opportunities.
Eligibility for doctoral study or advanced professional education.
Students should not assume that all programs called a master's or engineering course give the same qualification or recognition.

items: \\Possible mechanical engineering job titles:\\

Engineer, automotive.
Aerospace engineering
Engineer, Manufacturing.
Engineer in production.

Materials engineering.
Thermal systems engineer
Quality engineer.
Research & Development Engineer.
Your chances of getting a job will depend on your technical skills, work experience, language skills and work permit, as well as the specialization you choose.

\\Salaries for mechanical engineers in France\\ are affected by the employer, location, qualifications, industry and professional experience. Have students examine current job advertisements and salary surveys for particular engineering positions to determine possible pay.

faqs.q: Can I do a PG in Mechanical Engineering in France after BTech or BE?
faqs.a: Yes. Students pursuing \\BTech or BE in Mechanical Engineering\\ are eligible to apply for postgraduate courses in mechanical engineering, automotive engineering, manufacturing, material science or related fields. Admission is based on academic achievement and program specific requirements.

faqs.q: How long is PG in mechanical engineering in France?
faqs.a: In \\France\\, a \\national Master's degree\\ normally takes \\two years\\ of study following a relevant bachelor's degree. Some programs may allow suitably qualified candidates to enter directly into the second year.

faqs.q: Can I do PG mechanical engineering in France in English?
faqs.a: "Yes. Some French universities and engineering schools offer \\master's programs in mechanical engineering and related technical disciplines taught in English\\ Students are advised to check the language of instruction of the program of their choice.

faqs.q: What is the cost of mechanical engineering PG in France?
faqs.a: For \\2026-2027\\The public-university Master's reference fee is €255 per year for eligible French and EU students and €3,950 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. International specialized programs and private institutions may charge different fees.

faqs.q: What are the jobs after mechanical engineering PG in France?
faqs.a: Depending on their specialization and experience, graduates can work as \\mechanical design engineers\\, \\automotive engineers\\, \\aerospace engineers\\, \\manufacturing engineers\\, \\robotics engineers\\, \\mechatronics engineers\\ and \\research and development engineers.
